text: I'll be bound he'd be worth twenty pounds next spring.” The old gentleman laughed, and the little boy looked up eagerly. “Oh, grandpapa, did you not say the colt sold for five pounds more than you expected? You would not be poorer if you did buy this one.” The farmer slowly felt my legs, which were much swelled and strained; then he looked at my mouth. “Thirteen or fourteen, I should say; just trot him out, will you?” I arched my poor thin neck, raised my tail a little, and threw out my legs as well as I could, for they were very stiff. “What is the lowest you will take for him?” said the farmer as I came back.
